title: Emittance Minimization for Aberration Correction via Machine Learning and Bayesian Optimization
content: Precise control of the electron beam shape is critical for the successful application of scanning transmission electron microscopes (STEM) to understanding materials at atomic level. However, the nature of magnetic lenses introduces aberrations and and aberration correction is currently a complex and time-consuming procedure. Here we approach the problem from the perspective of accelerator physics by noting the equivalence between aberration correction and phase space beam emittance minimization [1]. We then show how a convolutional neural network (CNN) can be trained to predict beam emittance growth from Ronchigrams, enabling a one-to-one mapping served as the black-box function on which we apply Bayesian optimization (BO) to optimize for fully-automated aberration-corrector tuning [2].
